guides.title: Rituximab
guides.description: A B-cell-depleting antibody explored in a very small vitiligo pilot.

sections.label: Overview
sections.paragraph: Rituximab is used in specified B-cell cancers and autoimmune diseases. Its vitiligo evidence includes an uncontrolled five-person pilot.

sentences.text: Rituximab is used in specified B-cell cancers and autoimmune diseases.

sections.label: Benefits
sections.paragraph: Clinical evidence: Low. An uncontrolled vitiligo pilot treated five people with one rituximab infusion and followed them for six months. Three showed clear clinical and histological improvement, one slight improvement and one no change. Without a control group, this does not establish an average treatment effect, durability beyond follow-up or a validated retreatment schedule.

These precautions apply even when an investigated condition is not cancer.

guides.title: Memantine
guides.description: An NMDA-receptor blocker investigated for temozolomide resistance in glioblastoma cells.

sections.paragraph: Clinical evidence: Low for glioblastoma treatment. The cited experiment tested human glioblastoma cells, not patients. Memantine increased temozolomide-related cell injury while reducing MGMT, a DNA-repair protein. The study provides no patient survival, symptom or treatment-tolerability estimate; clinical benefit and a cancer regimen are not established by this cell experiment.

guides.title: Guanfacine
guides.description: An alpha-2A agonist investigated with N-acetylcysteine for Long COVID cognitive symptoms.

sections.label: Overview

sentences.text: Guanfacine extended release is an ADHD medicine.

sections.label: Benefits
sections.paragraph: Clinical evidence: Low. In an open-label series, eight of twelve people reported cognitive improvement with guanfacine plus N-acetylcysteine. Four stopped treatment: two for unspecified reasons and two for hypotension or dizziness. There was no placebo group or single-drug comparison, so the report cannot isolate guanfacine's effect or predict how often patients will improve.
